words.gloss: of hereditary, hired, guild, ally, enemy and forest-tribe troops

hindi: मौल, भृतक, श्रेणी, मित्र, अमित्र और आटवी सेनाओं को जुटाने के समय।
english: The occasions for mustering hereditary, hired, guild, ally, enemy and forest-tribe troops.
notes: The e-text '.' marks compound members. samuddāna = mustering/assembling (levying); Kangle 'mobilization'. Heading-like unit listing the six forces treated below.
lines_deva: मौल.भृतक.श्रेणी.मित्र.अमित्र.अटवी.बलानां समुद्दान.कालाः
lines_iast: maula.bhṛtaka.śreṇī.mitra.amitra.aṭavī.balānāṃ samuddāna.kālāḥ

words.gloss: because of ability to bear loss and expense
when the encounter is with much attached [troops]
from fear of the secret instigation by the one to be marched against
of the hired and the rest

hindi: जब मौल सेना मूल की रक्षा से अधिक हो, या अत्यावाप से युक्त मौल सैनिक मूल में विद्रोह कर सकें, या विरोधी की मौल सेना बहुत अनुरक्त हो अथवा उसकी सेना सार बल वाली हो, तब व्यायाम से लड़ना चाहिए; मार्ग लम्बा हो अथवा समय लम्बा हो तब मौल सैनिकों में क्षय और व्यय सहने की क्षमता होने से; बहुत अनुरक्त सेना से सामना होने पर, जिस पर चढ़ाई करनी है उसके उपजाप के भय से भृत आदि अन्य सेनाओं पर अविश्वास होने पर, अथवा सब सेनाओं की हानि होने पर — यह मौल सेना का समय है।
english: The hereditary troops are in excess of what is needed to guard the base; or the hereditary troops, provided with atyāvāpa [surplus addition], might rebel at the base; or the opponent has hereditary troops that are much attached, or has strong troops, [so that] one must fight with exertion; or the road or the time is long, because the hereditary troops can bear loss and expense; or when the encounter is with much attached [troops]; or when there is distrust of the other troops, the hired and the rest, from fear of secret instigation by the one to be marched against; or on a loss of troops among all the troops — [this is] the occasion for the hereditary troops.
notes: Long run-on sentence of conditions; the exact grammatical links are uncertain, so the conditions are listed as parallel. 'atyāvāpa' is a Book 10 term (surplus addition); here its sense 'surplus addition' is uncertain (alternative: excess of reinforcement/pay), rendered literally. 'bahula-anurakta-sampāte': I take sampāta as 'encounter'; low-medium confidence. 'vyāyāmena' = by exertion (fighting hard), per glossary Book 10. 'sāra-balo vā pratiyoddhā': 'or an opponent with strong troops' is also possible. 'mūla' = base (capital/home territory). The bare closing iti is not rendered. Review: 'atyāvāpa-yuktāḥ' (provided with surplus addition) and 'sampāta' (encounter) stay literal and doubtful. 'yātavyasya-upajāpa-bhayāt' is kept as one word in the draft although the printed hyphen joins yātavyasya and upajāpa-bhayāt (two words); a person may split it.
lines_deva: मूल.रक्षणाद् अतिरिक्तं मौल.बलम्, अत्यावाप.युक्ता वा मौला मूले विकुर्वीरन्, बहुल.अनुरक्त.मौल.बलः सार.बलो वा प्रतियोद्धा, व्यायामेन योद्धव्यम्, प्रकृष्टे ऽध्वनि काले वा क्षय.व्यय.सहत्वान् मौलानाम्, बहुल.अनुरक्त.सम्पाते च यातव्यस्य-उपजाप.भयाद् अन्य.सैन्यानां भृत.आदीनाम् अविश्वासे, बल.क्षये वा सर्व.सैन्यानाम् - इति मौल.बल.कालः
lines_iast: mūla.rakṣaṇād atiriktaṃ maula.balam, atyāvāpa.yuktā vā maulā mūle vikurvīran, bahula.anurakta.maula.balaḥ sāra.balo vā pratiyoddhā, vyāyāmena yoddhavyam, prakṛṣṭe 'dhvani kāle vā kṣaya.vyaya.sahatvān maulānām, bahula.anurakta.sampāte ca yātavyasya-upajāpa.bhayād anya.sainyānāṃ bhṛta.ādīnām aviśvāse, bala.kṣaye vā sarva.sainyānām - iti maula.bala.kālaḥ

hindi: “मेरी भृत सेना बहुत है और मौल सेना थोड़ी।” “शत्रु की मौल सेना थोड़ी है या विरक्त है, अथवा उसकी भृत सेना प्रायः दुर्बल है या सारहीन।” “मन्त्र से लड़ना चाहिए, थोड़े व्यायाम से।” “स्थान छोटा है या समय छोटा है, क्षय और व्यय थोड़ा है।” “मेरी सेना में आवाप थोड़ा है, उपजाप शान्त हो चुका है, या वह विश्वस्त है।” “शत्रु का प्रसार छोटा है, उसे नष्ट करना चाहिए।” — यह भृत सेना का समय है।
english: “My hired troops are abundant and the hereditary troops few.” “The enemy's hereditary troops are few or disaffected, or his hired army is mostly weak or without strength.” “One must fight by counsel, with little exertion.” “The place or the time is short, with little loss and expense.” “My army has little āvāpa, has its secret instigation quieted, or is trusted.” “The enemy's foraging force is small [and] is to be destroyed.” — [this is] the occasion for the hired troops.

notes: The editors' quote marks appear as 'ṇ' + '"' in the e-text, so each quotation ends with a stray ṇ; src kept as printed. 'parasya-alpam', 'parasya-alpaḥ': unsandhied joins, split into two words. 'prasāra' = the foraging force (glossary 10.2). The closing iti after the dash is not rendered; the copula is supplied in brackets. 'vyāyāma' = exertion in fighting. 'hrasvaḥ deśaḥ kālo vā' could also be read 'the (march) distance or time is short'.
lines_deva: "प्रभूतं मे भृत.बलम् अल्पं च मौल.बलम्ण्" "परस्य-अल्पं विरक्तं वा मौल.बलम्, फल्गु.प्रायम् असारं वा भृत.सैन्यम्ण्" "मन्त्रेण योद्धव्यम् अल्प.व्यायामेनण्" "ह्रस्वो देशः कालो वा तनु.क्षय.व्ययह्ण्" "अल्प.आवापं शान्त.उपजापं विश्वस्तं वा मे सैन्यम्ण्" "परस्य-अल्पः प्रसारो हन्तव्यह्ण्" - इति भृत.बल.कालः
lines_iast: "prabhūtaṃ me bhṛta.balam alpaṃ ca maula.balamṇ" "parasya-alpaṃ viraktaṃ vā maula.balam, phalgu.prāyam asāraṃ vā bhṛta.sainyamṇ" "mantreṇa yoddhavyam alpa.vyāyāmenaṇ" "hrasvo deśaḥ kālo vā tanu.kṣaya.vyayahṇ" "alpa.āvāpaṃ śānta.upajāpaṃ viśvastaṃ vā me sainyamṇ" "parasya-alpaḥ prasāro hantavyahṇ" - iti bhṛta.bala.kālaḥ

hindi: “मेरी श्रेणी सेना बहुत है; उसे मूल में और यात्रा में रखना सम्भव है।” प्रवास छोटा है; विरोधी अधिकतर श्रेणी सेना वाला है और मन्त्र तथा व्यायाम दोनों से लड़ना चाहता है; दण्ड और बल का व्यवहार है — यह श्रेणी सेना का समय है।
english: “My guild troops are abundant; it is possible to station [them] at the base and on the march.” The stay abroad is short; the opponent has mostly guild troops and wishes to fight back by counsel and exertion; the dealing is with army and troops — [this is] the occasion for the guild troops.

text_flags.why: stray ṇ before the closing quote

notes: 'daṇḍa-bala-vyavahāraḥ' is obscure; rendered literally (vyavahāra = dealing, conduct); alternatives: 'recourse to force and troops', or 'procedure of force-and-army fighting'. daṇḍa here is probably the force/army, not the array. pravāsa = being away from home (short campaign abroad). The subject of 'pratiyoddhu-kāmaḥ' is taken to be the opponent. The closing iti is not rendered. Review: the subject of 'pratiyoddhu-kāmaḥ' may be the king himself (desirous of fighting against the opponent) rather than the opponent; 'daṇḍa-bala-vyavahāraḥ' stays literal and doubtful.
lines_deva: "प्रभूतं मे श्रेणी.बलम्, शक्यं मूले यात्रायां च-आधातुम्ण्" ह्रस्वः प्रवासः, श्रेणी.बल.प्रायः प्रतियोद्धा मन्त्र.व्यायामाभ्यां प्रतियोद्धु.कामः, दण्ड.बल.व्यवहारः - इति श्रेणी.बल.कालः
lines_iast: "prabhūtaṃ me śreṇī.balam, śakyaṃ mūle yātrāyāṃ ca-ādhātumṇ" hrasvaḥ pravāsaḥ, śreṇī.bala.prāyaḥ pratiyoddhā mantra.vyāyāmābhyāṃ pratiyoddhu.kāmaḥ, daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāraḥ - iti śreṇī.bala.kālaḥ

hindi: “मेरी मित्र सेना बहुत है; उसे मूल में और यात्रा में रखना सम्भव है।” “प्रवास छोटा है और मन्त्रयुद्ध से व्यायाम-युद्ध अधिक है।” “अथवा पहले मित्र सेना से आटवी, नगर-स्थान या आसार को लड़वाकर फिर अपनी सेना से लड़ूँगा।” “अथवा मेरा कार्य मित्र के साथ साझा है।” “अथवा मेरे कार्य की सिद्धि मित्र पर निर्भर है।” “अथवा मेरा मित्र निकट है या अनुग्रह के योग्य है।” “अथवा उसके अत्यावाप को क्षीण करूँगा।” — यह मित्र सेना का समय है।
english: “My ally troops are abundant; it is possible to station [them] at the base and on the march.” “The stay abroad is short, and battle of exertion [is] greater than war of counsel.” “Or, having first made the ally troops fight the forest tribes, the town-station or the reinforcer, I shall afterwards fight with my own troops.” “Or my task is common with the ally.” “Or my success in the task depends on the ally.” “Or my ally is near or is one to be favoured.” “Or I shall wear down his atyāvāpa [surplus addition].” — [this is] the occasion for the ally troops.

words.gloss: of a dog and a boar
success of one or the other
time of war with the enemy and war with the inferior

hindi: “शत्रु की सेना मेरे पास बहुत है; मैं शत्रु की सेना से नगर-स्थान या आटवी को लड़ाऊँगा; वहाँ मेरे लिए कुत्ते और सूअर के झगड़े में चाण्डाल की तरह किसी एक की सिद्धि होगी।” “आसारों या आटवियों के काँटों का यह मर्दन मैं करूँगा।” — अथवा बहुत बढ़ी हुई, सदा निकट रहने वाली शत्रु की सेना को क्रोध के भय से बसाए, भीतरी कोप की आशंका को छोड़कर — और शत्रु से युद्ध तथा हीन से युद्ध का समय — यह अमित्र सेना का समय है।
english: “My enemy troops are abundant; with enemy troops I shall make the town-station or the forest tribes fight; there, as for a caṇḍāla in a quarrel between a dog and a boar, there will be success of one or the other for me.” “I shall do this crushing of the thorns of the reinforcers or of the forest tribes.” — Or he should lodge the enemy's troops, excessively grown and always near, from fear of anger, except where there is suspicion of internal revolt — and the time of war with the enemy and war with the inferior — [this is] the occasion for the enemy troops.

notes: Hard unit; the structure after the second quotation is uncertain. 'me śatru-balam' = my enemy troops (troops of the enemy at my disposal, or my troops against the enemy); literal. 'caṇḍāla' = outcaste, the proverb of the dog and boar fighting. 'kopa-bhayāt': kopa = anger; alternative 'fear of revolt' (cf. glossary 8.2). 'vāsayet' = he should lodge/settle (caus. of vas). 'avara-yuddha' = war with the inferior (or lesser war), uncertain. Whether 'śatru-yuddha-avara-yuddha-kālaḥ' is a further condition or a separate item is uncertain. Quote marks again as stray ṇ. Closing iti not rendered. Review: kopa in 'kopa-bhayāt' (rendered anger) and in 'abhyantara-kopa-śaṅkāyāḥ' (rendered revolt) may be one sense; the sentence after the second quotation (atyupacitam ... vāsayet, anyatra ..., and the time of war with the enemy and lesser war) is read tentatively. Confidence stays low.

hindi: मार्ग दिखाने वाली, पराई भूमि के योग्य, शत्रु के युद्ध के प्रतिकूल है; अथवा शत्रु अधिकतर आटवी सेना वाला है; “बिल्व को बिल्व से मारा जाए।” छोटे प्रसार को नष्ट करना चाहिए — यह आटवी सेना का समय है।
english: [They are] a guide on the road, suited to the enemy's ground, contrary to the enemy's way of fighting; or the enemy has mostly forest-tribe troops: “Let a bilva be struck by a bilva.” The small foraging force is to be destroyed — [this is] the occasion for the forest-tribe troops.

text_flags.why: stray ṇ before the closing quote

notes: 'mārga-ādeśikam' etc. are neuter singular adjectives with the subject (the forest troops) not stated; supplied in brackets. ādeśika = one who points out/directs (road-guide); alternative reading 'showing the way'. 'bilvaṃ bilvena hanyatām' is a proverb (bilva = the bilva fruit/tree); kept literal. 'prasāra' = the foraging force (glossary 10.2). Closing iti not rendered.

mostly alike in region, caste and craft

hindi: जो सेना अनेक हो, अनेक स्थानों में स्थित हो, कही गई हो या न कही गई हो, और लूट के लिए उठ खड़ी हो, वह औत्साहिक है — बिना भोजन और वेतन की, लूट, विष्टि और संताप करने वाली, दूसरों द्वारा तोड़ी जा सकने वाली; जो न तोड़ी जा सके वह अधिकतर समान देश, जाति और शिल्प वाली, संगठित और बड़ी होती है। ॥९॥ ये सेना को ग्रहण करने के समय हैं।
english: An army that is many, stationed in many places, stated or unstated, and rises for the sake of plunder, that is the autsāhika: without rations and wages, causing plunder, forced labour and burning, divisible by the others; the indivisible [kind] is mostly alike in region, caste and craft, united, large. 9. [These are] the occasions for taking up troops.
notes: Obscure: 'autsāhika' (from utsāha, energy/enterprise) kept as a name; 'abhakta-vetanam' = without rations and wages (bhakta = food/ration, vetana = wages); 'pratāpa' = literally 'heat, burning'; alternatives: distress, might; low confidence. 'uktam anuktaṃ vā' = stated or unstated; what is stated is not given. 'bhedyaṃ pareṣām' could also be 'divisible by others'. The sentence is read as: the autsāhika army is the divisible kind, the indivisible kind is the united one; the grammar is loose, so the reading is tentative. 'vilopa-artham' = for the sake of plunder. The closing 'iti ... kālāḥ' is not rendered 'thus'; copula supplied in brackets. The ' | 9 | ' tokens are the verse-number marks; the unit may be a closing summary of the chapter. Review: 'viṣṭi' here may be forced labour or the labour corps, and 'pratāpa' (burning/might) is doubtful; 'aneka-stha' literally 'standing in many', 'places' is supplied. Confidence stays low.
lines_deva: सैन्यम् अनेकम् अनेकस्थम् उक्तम् अनुक्तं वा विलोप.अर्थं यद् उत्तिष्ठति तद् औत्साहिकं - अभक्त.वेतनं विलोप.विष्टि.प्रताप.करं भेद्यं परेषाम्, अभेद्यं तुल्य.देश.जाति.शिल्प.प्रायं संहतं महत् । ९ । इति बल.उपादान.कालाह्
lines_iast: sainyam anekam anekastham uktam anuktaṃ vā vilopa.arthaṃ yad uttiṣṭhati tad autsāhikaṃ - abhakta.vetanaṃ vilopa.viṣṭi.pratāpa.karaṃ bhedyaṃ pareṣām, abhedyaṃ tulya.deśa.jāti.śilpa.prāyaṃ saṃhataṃ mahat | 9 | iti bala.upādāna.kālāh

hindi: उनमें से शत्रु और आटवी सेना को कुप्य से भृत या लूट से भृत करे।
english: Of these, he should make the enemy and forest-tribe troops hired with raw materials or hired with plunder.
notes: kupya = raw materials (glossary). 'teṣām' = of these (the six kinds of troops); the exact partitive is uncertain. 'amitra-aṭavī-balam' is read as one dvandva of the enemy and forest-tribe troops; alternative: the enemy's forest-tribe troops.
lines_deva: तेषां कुप्य.भृतम् अमित्र.अटवी.बलं विलोप.भृतं वा कुर्यात्
lines_iast: teṣāṃ kupya.bhṛtam amitra.aṭavī.balaṃ vilopa.bhṛtaṃ vā kuryāt

hindi: अथवा शत्रु की सेना का समय आ पड़ने पर शत्रु की सेना को रोक ले, या अन्यत्र भेज दे, या निष्फल कर दे, या बिखरी हुई बसाए, या समय बीत जाने पर छोड़ दे।
english: Or, when the occasion for the enemy's troops has arisen, he should restrain the enemy troops, or send them elsewhere, or make them fruitless, or lodge them scattered, or dismiss them when the time has passed.
notes: 'amitrasya ... bala-kāle' read as 'the occasion for the enemy's troops'; alternative: the occasion of the enemy's troops (the time when the enemy musters). 'avagṛhṇīyāt' = restrain/hold back (alternative: seize). 'vāsayet' = lodge/settle, as in unit 6. The objects 'them' are supplied by the verb construction.
lines_deva: अमित्रस्य वा बल.काले प्रत्युत्पन्ने शत्रु.बलम् अवगृह्णीयात्, अन्यत्र वा प्रेषयेत्, अफलं वा कुर्यात्, विक्षिप्तं वा वासयेत्, काले वा-अतिक्रान्ते विसृजेत्
lines_iast: amitrasya vā bala.kāle pratyutpanne śatru.balam avagṛhṇīyāt, anyatra vā preṣayet, aphalaṃ vā kuryāt, vikṣiptaṃ vā vāsayet, kāle vā-atikrānte visṛjet

hindi: शत्रु के इस सेना-संग्रह को वह विफल करे और अपने लिए सम्पन्न करे।
english: He should frustrate this mustering of troops of the enemy, and bring [it] about for himself.
notes: 'ca-etat' is an unsandhied join of ca and etat. 'ātmanaḥ' = of himself / for himself (genitive of interest). Object of sampādayet is supplied in brackets in English.
lines_deva: परस्य च-एतद् बल.समुद्दानं विघातयेत्, आत्मनः सम्पादयेत्
lines_iast: parasya ca-etad bala.samuddānaṃ vighātayet, ātmanaḥ sampādayet

hindi: और इनमें से पूर्व-पूर्व को सज्जित करना श्रेष्ठ है।
english: And of these, each earlier one is better to mobilise.
notes: 'pūrvaṃ pūrvam' repeated = each earlier one in turn, i.e. in the order of the six kinds listed in unit 1 (hereditary first). 'samnāhayitum' = to mobilise/equip for war (inf. of caus. sam-√nah).
lines_deva: पूर्वं पूर्वं च-एषां श्रेयः सम्नाहयितुम्
lines_iast: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca-eṣāṃ śreyaḥ samnāhayitum

words.gloss: because of partaking of that state
because of constant honour and attendance

hindi: उसी भाव को पाने वाले होने के कारण और नित्य सत्कार तथा अनुसरण के कारण मौल सेना भृत सेना से श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Because of partaking of that state, and because of constant honour and attendance, the hereditary troops are better than the hired troops.
notes: 'tad-bhāva-bhāvitvāt' is obscure: 'tad' presumably refers to the king's own condition or fortunes (so: sharing his condition), but this is not stated; rendered literally. 'nitya-satkāra-anugamāt': anugama can be 'following/attendance' or 'compliance'. Low-medium on this phrase.
lines_deva: तद्.भाव.भावित्वान् नित्य.सत्कार.अनुगमाच् च मौल.बलं भृत.बलात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: tad.bhāva.bhāvitvān nitya.satkāra.anugamāc ca maula.balaṃ bhṛta.balāt-śreyaḥ

hindi: नित्य निकट रहने वाली, शीघ्र उठ खड़ी होने वाली अथवा वश में रहने वाली भृत सेना श्रेणी सेना से श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The hired troops, constantly adjacent, quick to rise, or controllable, are better than the guild troops.

text_flags.why: possible typo: short a for long ā; sense requires the particle vā (or)

notes: 'nitya-anantaram' is uncertain: literally 'always immediately next/adjacent'; alternatives: always next in order, or always readily at hand. 'vaśyam' = under control, obedient. 'va' read as vā 'or' (possible; if truly 'va' it would be 'eva'-like and the line would read 'and indeed controllable'). Review: since the three qualities of the hired troops are cumulative, the printed 'va' may stand for 'ca' (and) rather than vā (or); draft reading vā kept, a person should decide.
lines_deva: नित्य.अनन्तरं क्षिप्र.उत्थायि वश्यं व भृत.बलं श्रेणी.बलात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: nitya.anantaraṃ kṣipra.utthāyi vaśyaṃ va bhṛta.balaṃ śreṇī.balāt-śreyaḥ

words.gloss: having alike rivalry, indignation, success and gain

hindi: जनपद की, एक ही प्रयोजन को प्राप्त हुई, और समान संघर्ष, अमर्ष, सिद्धि और लाभ वाली श्रेणी सेना मित्र सेना से श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The guild troops, being of the country, come to one purpose, and having alike rivalry, indignation, success and gain, are better than the ally troops.
notes: 'jānapadam' = of the country (people); the glossary renders jānapada (people) as country people, so the adjective is rendered 'of the country'. 'saṅgharṣa' = rivalry/ardour and 'amarṣa' = indignation/intolerance are literal and uncertain in this context.
lines_deva: जानपदम् एक.अर्थ.उपगतं तुल्य.सङ्घर्ष.अमर्ष.सिद्धि.लाभं च श्रेणी.बलं मित्र.बलात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: jānapadam eka.artha.upagataṃ tulya.saṅgharṣa.amarṣa.siddhi.lābhaṃ ca śreṇī.balaṃ mitra.balāt-śreyaḥ

words.gloss: because of coming to one purpose

hindi: असीमित देश और काल वाली तथा एक ही प्रयोजन को प्राप्त होने के कारण मित्र सेना शत्रु सेना से श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The ally troops, of unlimited place and time, and because of coming to one purpose, are better than the enemy troops.
notes: 'aparimita-deśa-kālam' read as bahuvrīhi describing the ally troops (not limited in place or time of service).
lines_deva: अपरिमित.देश.कालम् एक.अर्थ.उपगमाच् च मित्र.बलम् अमित्र.बलात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: aparimita.deśa.kālam eka.artha.upagamāc ca mitra.balam amitra.balāt-śreyaḥ

words.gloss: presided over by a noble man

hindi: आर्य द्वारा अधिष्ठित शत्रु की सेना आटवी सेना से श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Enemy troops presided over by a noble man (ārya) are better than forest-tribe troops.
notes: 'ārya' = noble man (alternative: an Aryan, i.e. a man of the twice-born classes); kept as 'noble man (ārya)'. adhiṣṭhita = presided over / commanded.
lines_deva: आर्य.अधिष्ठितम् अमित्र.बलम् अटवी.बलात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: ārya.adhiṣṭhitam amitra.balam aṭavī.balāt-śreyaḥ

hindi: वे दोनों लूट के लिए हैं।
english: Those two are for the sake of plunder.
notes: 'tad ubhayam' = those two (the enemy troops and the forest-tribe troops of the previous unit).
lines_deva: तद् उभयं विलोप.अर्थम्
lines_iast: tad ubhayaṃ vilopa.artham

hindi: लूट न होने पर और व्यसन में उन दोनों से साँप का भय हो सकता है।
english: When there is no plunder, and in calamity, there would be fear of a snake from those two.
notes: 'ahi-bhayam' = fear of a snake, rendered literally (a figure for danger from those two); alternative 'fear from a snake'. vyasana = calamity (glossary 8.1).
lines_deva: अविलोपे व्यसने च ताभ्याम् अहि.भयं स्यात्
lines_iast: avilope vyasane ca tābhyām ahi.bhayaṃ syāt

words.gloss: of the troops of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras
because of the predominance of energy

hindi: “ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य और शूद्र की सेनाओं में तेज की प्रधानता के कारण पूर्व-पूर्व को सज्जित करना श्रेष्ठ है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: “Of the troops of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, because of the predominance of energy, each earlier one is better to mobilise,” say the teachers.
notes: tejas = energy/brilliance (alternative: spirit, fiery vigour). Formula '... iti X' = '...,' say X (glossary). 'ācāryāḥ' = the teachers (unnamed authorities).
lines_deva: "ब्राह्मण.क्षत्रिय.वैश्य.शूद्र.सैन्यानां तेजः.प्राधान्यात् पूर्वं पूर्वं श्रेयः सम्नाहयितुम्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "brāhmaṇa.kṣatriya.vaiśya.śūdra.sainyānāṃ tejaḥ.prādhānyāt pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ śreyaḥ samnāhayitum" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
notes: Glossary formula 'na iti X'.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: शत्रु प्रणिपात से ब्राह्मणों की सेना को अपनी ओर ले आ सकता है।
english: The enemy might bring over the Brahmin troops by prostration.
notes: 'abhihārayet' (caus. of abhi-√hṛ) is rendered 'bring over'; alternatives: carry off, win over, attack. 'paraḥ' = the enemy (other party). The e-text gives 'paro 'bhihārayet' with avagraha; src kept as printed.
lines_deva: प्रणिपातेन ब्राह्मण.बलं परो ऽभिहारयेत्
lines_iast: praṇipātena brāhmaṇa.balaṃ paro 'bhihārayet

words.gloss: trained in the science of weapons

hindi: किन्तु शस्त्र-विद्या में प्रशिक्षित क्षत्रिय सेना श्रेष्ठ है, अथवा बहुत सार वाली वैश्य और शूद्र सेना।
english: But Kshatriya troops trained in the science of weapons are better, or Vaishya and Shudra troops of abundant strength.
notes: The closing iti is not rendered. Whether this is the continuation of Kautilya's view after unit 22 (so closed by iti) is uncertain; no opening quote is printed. 'sāra' = strength/ best part (glossary 10.3 'sāra-bala' = best troops); here 'abundant strength'. Hindi 'प्रशिक्षित' for vinīta.
lines_deva: प्रहरण.विद्या.विनीतं तु क्षत्रिय.बलं श्रेयः, बहुल.सारं वा वैश्य.शूद्र.बलम् इति
lines_iast: praharaṇa.vidyā.vinītaṃ tu kṣatriya.balaṃ śreyaḥ, bahula.sāraṃ vā vaiśya.śūdra.balam iti

hindi: इसलिए “शत्रु ऐसी सेना वाला है; यह उसका प्रतिबल है” — सेना का संग्रह करे।
english: Therefore: “The enemy has troops of this kind; this is the counterforce to him” — he should make the mustering of troops.
notes: The closing iti marks the content of the thought and is rendered only by the quotation marks. 'tasya-etat' = unsandhied join. pratibala = counterforce, counterpart troops.
lines_deva: तस्माद् एवं.बलः परः, तस्य-एतत् प्रतिबलम् इति बल.समुद्दानं कुर्यात्
lines_iast: tasmād evaṃ.balaḥ paraḥ, tasya-etat pratibalam iti bala.samuddānaṃ kuryāt

words.gloss: provided with elephant-machines(?), carts, garbha, lances, javelins, hāṭaka, bamboo and darts

hindi: हस्ति-यन्त्र, शकट, गर्भ, कुन्त, प्रास, हाटक, वेणु और शल्य से युक्त सेना हाथियों की सेना का प्रतिबल है।
english: [A force] provided with hasti-yantra, carts, garbha, lances, javelins, hāṭaka, bamboo and darts is the counterforce to the elephant troops.
notes: Obscure compound. The members are taken as a list: hasti-yantra (literally 'elephant-machine'; sense uncertain), śakaṭa = cart, garbha (kept; sense uncertain), kunta = lance, prāsa = javelin, hāṭaka (kept; literally 'gold'; sense uncertain), veṇu = bamboo, śalya = dart/spike; -vat = provided with. Alternatives: hasti-yantra-śakaṭa could be one item (elephant-machine carts); 'garbha' and 'hāṭaka' may be technical weapon or device names. The subject '[a force]' is supplied in brackets (English only).
lines_deva: हस्ति.यन्त्र.शकट.गर्भ.कुन्त.प्रास.हाटक.वेणु.शल्यवद् हस्ति.बलस्य प्रतिबलम्
lines_iast: hasti.yantra.śakaṭa.garbha.kunta.prāsa.hāṭaka.veṇu.śalyavad hasti.balasya pratibalam

words.gloss: consisting mostly of stones, clubs, coverings, goads and hair-seizers

hindi: वही, जिसमें अधिकतर पत्थर, लाठी, आवरण, अंकुश और केश-ग्रहणी हों, रथ-सेना का प्रतिबल है।
english: That very [force], consisting mostly of stones, clubs, coverings, goads and hair-seizers, is the counterforce to the chariot troops.
notes: 'kaca-grahaṇī' (literally 'hair-seizer', fem. noun) is a device of uncertain sense; kept literal. 'āvaraṇa' = covering/shield; uncertain. 'tad eva' refers to the force of the previous unit. The compound could also read 'kaca-grahaṇī' as 'hair-grasping [hooks]'.
lines_deva: तद् एव पाषाण.लगुड.आवरण.अङ्कुश.कच.ग्रहणी.प्रायं रथ.बलस्य प्रतिबलम्
lines_iast: tad eva pāṣāṇa.laguḍa.āvaraṇa.aṅkuśa.kaca.grahaṇī.prāyaṃ ratha.balasya pratibalam

hindi: वही घोड़ों का प्रतिबल है, अथवा कवचधारी हाथी या कवचधारी घोड़े।
english: That very [force] is the counterforce to horses; or armoured elephants, or armoured horses.
notes: 'tad eva' refers to the force described in the previous unit. 'varmiṇaḥ' = wearing armour, qualifying both hastinaḥ and aśvāḥ.
lines_deva: तद् एव-अश्वानां प्रतिबलम्, वर्मिणो वा हस्तिनो ऽश्वा वा वर्मिणः
lines_iast: tad eva-aśvānāṃ pratibalam, varmiṇo vā hastino 'śvā vā varmiṇaḥ

hindi: कवचधारी रथ और आवरण वाले पैदल सैनिक चतुरंग सेना का प्रतिबल हैं।
english: Armoured chariots and foot-soldiers with coverings are the counterforce to the fourfold army.
notes: 'āvaraṇinaḥ' = provided with coverings (āvaraṇa, as in unit 27); 'with shields' is a likely sense but not stated. 'catur-aṅga-bala' = the fourfold army (glossary 10.4).
lines_deva: कवचिनो रथा आवरणिनः पत्तयश् च चतुर्.अङ्ग.बलस्य प्रतिबलम्
lines_iast: kavacino rathā āvaraṇinaḥ pattayaś ca catur.aṅga.balasya pratibalam

hindi: इस प्रकार सेना का संग्रह, जो शत्रु की सेना को रोकना है, वह अपने साधन से अपनी सेनाओं के अंगों के विकल्प के अनुसार करे।
english: Thus the mustering of troops, the warding off of the enemy's army: he should carry it out with [his] resources, for his own troops, by options of the arms [of the army].
notes: The syntax is loose: 'bala-samuddāna' and 'para-sainya-nivāraṇa' are read together as the object of 'kuryāt'. 'vibhavena' = by means/resources (alternative: according to his power). 'sva-sainyānām' = of one's own troops, construed with the mustering. 'aṅga-vikalpaśaḥ' = by option of the arms (the four arms or the six classes); sense uncertain. Hindi 'इस प्रकार' renders evam (thus), allowed here as it is a Sanskrit word. Review: 'vibhavena sva-sainyānām' may instead mean 'according to the means of his own troops'; draft construction kept.
lines_deva: एवं बल.समुद्दानं पर.सैन्य.निवारणम्
विभवेन स्व.सैन्यानां कुर्याद् अङ्ग.विकल्पशः
lines_iast: evaṃ bala.samuddānaṃ para.sainya.nivāraṇam
vibhavena sva.sainyānāṃ kuryād aṅga.vikalpaśaḥ
